items.title: Warren Bernhardt interviewed by Monk Rowe, Bearsville, New York, January 3, 2012
items.q: she looks down at me after the concert and said I’d like to play an encore for a really good young friend of mine, and points to me.

ctx.x: In my pajamas, you know. Yeah. A lot of guys, a lot of guys. But I mean it was that era where mistakes were okay. There was about 150 years in there where the critics didn’t mind that as long as the heart and the correct feeling and the awesomeness of it all came through. What’s a mistake? Oh he forgot. I remember I got a good lesson, I was learning a toccata by Paradisi in A major. It’s a simple piece but it’s not simple. It’s a lot of answering response and answering the different hands. And toccata means…

and I played the toccata for her, and I was just learning it, and stumbling through it. So and that was on a Friday night. And Sunday afternoon we went to hear her at Town Hall and I was like in the fifth row or something, and she looks down at me after the concert and said I’d like to play an encore for a really good young friend of mine, and points to me. And she sits down and plays the toccata and she spaces out and forgets where she is. I mean she really lost it. She couldn’t get it back. Then she apologized…
